literature.headline_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期乙型肝炎病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 基线分析结果:与普遍接种出生剂量策略(255例儿童感染 [95% 置信区间,130至530])相比,延迟接种和共享决策策略将使2026年出生的队列研究地区的慢性HBV感染人数分别增加19%至303(95% 置信区间,155至610)和83%至467(95% 置信区间,209至1032)。这些策略还将使20年后的HBV易感人群数量分别增加至474 000和1 806 000,相比普遍接种出生剂量策略的232 000。 [10.7326/annals-26-02135]

在180名HCT前anti-HBc阴性的患者中,有6名(3.3%)在HCT后anti-HBc转为阳性。在164名HCT前anti-HBs阴性的患者中,有49名(29.9%)在HCT后anti-HBs转为阳性。所有新检测到抗体的患者均保持HBsAg阴性,且可获得的HBV DNA检测结果未显示有活动性HBV感染的证据。在后续随访检测中,3名可评估的患者在中位数240天后anti-HBc消失,而32名可评估患者中,有30名(93.8%)在中位数119天后anti-HBs水平下降或消失。 [10.1111/trf.70448]
EP、EN和HC组的α多样性和β多样性均无显著差异。种群水平分析发现,与Bacteroidales和Firmicutes相关的厌氧共生菌存在组间差异,但这些差异在全局FDR校正后均不显著。在EN组中,选定的菌群在下采样、留一法和CLR基础上的敏感性分析中显示出方向一致的关联,但这些发现同样在FDR校正后不显著。 [10.1128/spectrum.03896-25]
HDV-HCC患者年龄较小,肝功能受损更严重,AST、CRP和白细胞水平较低。HDV-HCC肿瘤体积较小,门静脉浸润较少见,且更常符合米兰标准。全身免疫特征分析显示HDV-HCC和HBV-HCC之间存在不同的炎症模式。 [10.1097/hc9.0000000000001060]
在FDR校正后,HCs与MHE之间有21个区域标签存在差异,HCs与NMHE之间有21个区域标签存在差异,而MHE与NMHE之间没有区域标签存在差异。 [10.21203/rs.3.rs-11096469/v1]

literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: RESULTS OF BASE-CASE ANALYSIS: Compared with the universal birth-dose strategy (255 childhood infections [95% UI, 130 to 530]), the deferred and shared decision-making strategies would increase chronic HBV infections in the 2026 birth cohort by 19% to 303 (95% UI, 155 to 610) and by 83% to 467 (95% UI, 209 to 1032), respectively. [10.7326/annals-26-02135]

Among 180 patients who were anti-HBc negative before HCT, 6 (3.3%) developed anti-HBc positivity after HCT. Among 164 patients who were anti-HBs negative before HCT, 49 (29.9%) developed anti-HBs positivity. [10.1111/trf.70448]

Active infection prevalence was 136.2 per 100,000 donors (95% CI, 131.2-141.3) for HBV and 57.4 (95% CI, 53.8-61.1) for HCV. Incidence rates were 3.54 (95% CI, 3.01-4.11) and 3.99 (95% CI, 3.33-4.72) per 100,000 person-years, respectively. Prevalence decreased annually by 7.6% for HBV and 11.0% for HCV. [10.1111/trf.70446]

Alpha and beta diversity did not differ significantly among EP, EN, and HC groups. Species-level analyses identified nominal group-related differences in several Bacteroidales- and Firmicutes-associated anaerobic commensals, but none remained significant after global FDR correction. [10.1128/spectrum.03896-25]

HDV-HCC patients were younger, had more impaired liver function, and lower levels of AST, CRP, and leukocytes. HDV-HCC tumors were smaller, less frequently infiltrated, and more often fulfilled Milan criteria. Systemic immune profiling revealed distinct inflammatory patterns between HDV-HCC and HBV-HCC. [10.1097/hc9.0000000000001060]

papers.title: Global Underutilization of Antiviral Therapy and Survival Outcomes in Hepatitis B Virus-Related Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of 78 Studies and 68,243 Patients.
papers.abstract: Antiviral therapy with nucleos(t)ide analogues is recommended for patients with viremic hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related cirrhosis regardless of levels of viremia or liver enzymes. However, hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is not an antiviral treatment criterion in the U.S. HBV treatment guidelines, though prior studies have reported improved survival with antiviral treatment in HBV-related HCC. To inform guidelines, we estimated antiviral treatment rates and their association with survival and HCC recurrence rates in HBV-related HCC. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies published between 2006 and 2024 that reported antiviral treatment, survival, and/or HCC recurrence rates in adults with HBV-related HCC, following PRISMA guidelines. Random-effects models pooled study estimates. Of the initial 4556 studies, 178 underwent full-text review, and 78 (68,243 patients) were analysed. The pooled antiviral treatment rate (52 studies, 41,345 patients) was 53.1%. In studies reporting pre-HCC antiviral initiation, 17.2% of HBV-related HCC patients received therapy before diagnosis. Treated (vs untreated) patients had higher 3- and 5-year OS (80.4% vs. 46.8%, both p < 0.01). Five-year OS was 78.0% vs. 56.4% in inactive HCC (p < 0.01) and 48.2% vs. 22.6% in active HCC (p = 0.14). Antiviral therapy remained independently associated with improved 5-year OS in multivariable meta-regression. There was no significant difference in HCC recurrence rates. Antiviral therapy is associated with improved long-term survival but remains underutilized in HBV-related HCC. These findings highlight a critical gap in care and underscore the need for earlier and more consistent antiviral initiation in patients with HBV-related HCC.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the global underutilization of antiviral therapy in patients with hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and its impact on survival outcomes. The central question is whether antiviral therapy improves survival in HBV-related HCC and how its utilization varies across populations.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a systematic analysis and meta-analysis of 78 studies involving 68,243 patients, published between 2006 and 2024. The initial search identified 4556 studies, of which 178 underwent full-text review.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Antiviral therapy with nucleos(t)ide analogues is associated with improved long-term survival in HBV-related HCC. Treated patients had higher 3- and 5-year overall survival (OS) rates compared to untreated patients. analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is no significant difference in HCC recurrence rates between treated and untreated patients. analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings emphasize the need for updating clinical guidelines to include HCC as an antiviral treatment criterion. analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 78 studies involving 68,243 patients examines the underutilization of antiviral therapy in hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and its impact on survival. The review found that antiviral therapy is associated with improved 3- and 5-year overall survival rates in HBV-related HCC, with treated patients showing higher survival compared to untreated ones. However, only 17.2% of patients received antiviral therapy before HCC diagnosis, highlighting a critical gap in care. The study also notes no significant difference in HCC recurrence rates between treated and untreated patients, suggesting the need for more consistent and earlier antiviral initiation in clinical practice. These findings underscore the importance of revising guidelines to incorporate HCC as a criterion for antiviral treatment and call for further research to optimize treatment strategies.

papers.abstract_zh: 使用核苷(酸)类似物进行抗病毒药物治疗被推荐用于所有具有病毒血症的乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)相关肝硬化的患者,无论其病毒载量或肝酶水平如何。然而,肝细胞癌(HCC)并不是美国HBV 治疗指南中的治疗标准。尽管之前的研究报告指出,在HBV相关HCC患者中,抗病毒药物治疗与改善生存率相关,但目前仍缺乏明确的指南。为了指导指南制定,我们估计了抗病毒药物治疗率及其与生存率和HCC复发率之间的关联。我们按照PRISMA指南,对2006年至2024年间发表的、报告了HBV相关HCC成人患者抗病毒药物治疗率、生存率和/或HCC复发率的研究进行了系统综述和荟萃分析。使用随机效应模型汇总研究估计值。初始共有4556项研究,其中178项进行了全文审查,最终分析了78项(共68,243名患者)。汇总的抗病毒药物治疗率(52项研究,41,345名患者)为53.1%。在报告了HCC前抗病毒药物治疗启动的研究中,17.2%的HBV相关HCC患者在HCC发生前接受了治疗。接受治疗(与未接受治疗相比)的患者3年和5年总生存率(OS)更高(80.4% vs. 46.8%,两者p < 0.01)。在非活动性HCC研究中,5年OS为78.0% vs. 56.4%(p < 0.01),而在活动性HCC研究中,5年OS为48.2% vs. 22.6%(p = 0.14)。在多变量荟萃回归分析中,抗病毒药物治疗仍与改善5年OS独立相关。HCC复发率没有显著差异。抗病毒药物治疗与改善长期生存率相关,但在HBV相关HCC中仍被低估使用。这些发现突显了护理中的关键差距,并强调了在HBV相关HCC患者中更早和更一致地启动抗病毒药物治疗的必要性。

analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 治疗组与未治疗组在HCC复发率方面无显著差异。此外,综述还指出在护理方面存在关键缺口,建议需要更早且更一致地启动抗病毒药物疗法。证据还表明,抗病毒药物疗法与生存率之间的关联可能因HCC的活动性而有所不同。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 研究结果强调需要更新临床指南,将HCC纳入抗病毒药物治疗的考虑因素。还需要进一步研究以确定HBV相关HCC中抗病毒药物疗法的最佳时机和持续时间,并解决不同HCC亚型中治疗结局的差异性。}}.{

papers.title: Similar Long-Term Incidence of Hepatocellular Carcinoma in Chronic Hepatitis B Initiating Entecavir Versus Tenofovir Alafenamide: A REAL-B Study.
papers.abstract: Data on potential differences in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) incidence between entecavir (ETV) and tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) patients are limited. This retrospective multinational study included treatment-naïve adults with CHB without a history of HCC who initiated ETV or TAF therapy since 2016 at 23 centres in 4 countries. Baseline characteristics were balanced using inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and propensity score matching (PSM). HCC incidence and the association between antiviral regimen and HCC were analysed using competing-risk analysis. A total of 1437 patients (710 ETV, 727 TAF) were included, with similar mean follow-up durations (55.5 ± 29.8 vs. 58.0 ± 25.5 months; p = 0.077). ETV-treated patients were older, more frequently male, and more likely to have cirrhosis. After IPTW, both groups had balanced characteristics (all standardised differences < 0.1). After IPTW adjustment, during follow-up, 23 patients on ETV and 20 on TAF developed HCC, with incidence rates of 0.67 and 0.65 per 100 person-years, respectively (p = 0.853). There was no statistically significant difference in HCC risk between the groups (SHR: 1.09; 95% CI: 0.44-2.65; p = 0.851), with consistent findings across subgroups by age, sex, cirrhosis, hepatic steatosis, HBeAg, baseline liver enzymes, HBV DNA levels, diabetes mellitus and in sensitivity analysis using PSM. In this real-world multinational study of treatment-naïve CHB patients, HCC incidence did not significantly differ between ETV and TAF groups, suggesting therapeutic selection should consider cost and patient-specific factors.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to evaluate the long-term incidence of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) patients initiating entecavir (ETV) or tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) therapy. A retrospective multinational analysis of 1437 treatment-naïve adults with CHB without prior HCC was conducted across 23 centres in four countries. Baseline characteristics were balanced using inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and propensity score matching (PSM). The study found that 23 patients on ETV and 20 on TAF developed HCC during follow-up, with incidence rates of 0.67 and 0.65 per 100 person-years, respectively. The findings suggest that therapeutic selection should consider cost and patient-specific factors rather than HCC risk. However, the study noted that ETV-treated patients were older, more frequently male, and more likely to have cirrhosis, which may introduce potential biases.

papers.title_zh: 恩替卡韦与替诺福韦艾拉酚胺在慢性乙型肝炎患者中对肝细胞癌长期发病率的比较:REAL-B研究
papers.source_body_en: Data on potential differences in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) incidence between entecavir (ETV) and tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) patients are limited. This retrospective multinational study included treatment-naïve adults with CHB without a history of HCC who initiated ETV or TAF therapy since 2016 at 23 centres in 4 countries. Baseline characteristics were balanced using inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and propensity score matching (PSM). HCC incidence and the association between antiviral regimen and HCC were analysed using competing-risk analysis. A total of 1437 patients (710 ETV, 727 TAF) were included, with similar mean follow-up durations (55.5 ± 29.8 vs. 58.0 ± 25.5 months; p = 0.077). ETV-treated patients were older, more frequently male, and more likely to have cirrhosis. After IPTW, both groups had balanced characteristics (all standardised differences < 0.1). After IPTW adjustment, during follow-up, 23 patients on ETV and 20 on TAF developed HCC, with incidence rates of 0.67 and 0.65 per 100 person-years, respectively (p = 0.853). There was no statistically significant difference in HCC risk between the groups (SHR: 1.09; 95% CI: 0.44-2.65; p = 0.851), with consistent findings across subgroups by age, sex, cirrhosis, hepatic steatosis, HBeAg, baseline liver enzymes, HBV DNA levels, diabetes mellitus and in sensitivity analysis using PSM. In this real-world multinational study of treatment-naïve CHB patients, HCC incidence did not significantly differ between ETV and TAF groups, suggesting therapeutic selection should consider cost and patient-specific factors.
papers.abstract_zh: 关于恩替卡韦(ETV)和替诺福韦艾拉酚胺(TAF)在慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)患者中对肝细胞癌(HCC)发病率潜在差异的数据有限。本回顾性多国研究纳入了2016年以来在4个国家的23个中心开始接受ETV或TAF治疗的、无HCC病史且未接受过抗病毒药物治疗的CHB成人患者。使用逆概率加权(IPTW)和倾向评分匹配(PSM)方法平衡基线特征。采用竞争风险分析方法分析HCC发病率及抗病毒治疗方案与HCC之间的关联。共纳入1437名患者(ETV组710名,TAF组727名),其平均随访时间相似(ETV组55.5 ± 29.8个月 vs. TAF组58.0 ± 25.5个月;p = 0.077)。接受ETV治疗的患者年龄更大,男性比例更高,且更可能患有肝硬化。在IPTW调整后,两组患者的特征趋于平衡(所有标准化差异均<0.1)。调整后随访期间,ETV组有23例患者和TAF组有20例患者发展为HCC,其HCC发病率分别为每100人年0.67和0.65(p = 0.853)。两组之间HCC风险无统计学显著差异(SHR:1.09;95% CI:0.44-2.65;p = 0.851),且在按年龄、性别、肝硬化、脂肪肝、HBeAg状态、基线肝酶水平、HBV DNA水平、糖尿病等亚组分析以及使用PSM进行敏感性分析中结果一致。在这一真实世界多国研究中,对于未接受过抗病毒治疗的CHB患者,ETV和TAF组的HCC发病率无显著差异,提示治疗选择应考虑成本和患者个体因素。

papers.title: Safety, Tolerability and Antiviral Activity of GST-HG131 in Chronic Hepatitis B: A Randomized, Double-Blind Phase IIa Study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains a major global health burden. Current therapies rarely achieve a functional cure due to low rates of HBsAg clearance, the persistence of the viral replication template-covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA)-and the need for lifelong treatment. GST-HG131 is a first-in-class, orally bioavailable small-molecule inhibitor of PAPD5/7, key host factors involved in HBV mRNA stabilization and HBsAg production. We evaluated the safety, tolerability and antiviral activity of GST-HG131 in patients with CHB receiving nucleos(t)ide analogue (NUC) therapy in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase IIa study. METHODS: This double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled Phase IIa study evaluated the efficacy and safety of GST-HG131 in 45 CHB patients. Cohorts 1 and 2 (n = 10 each; 8 active, 2 placebo) received 30 mg or 60 mg BID for 28 days, respectively. Cohort 3 (n = 25; 20 active, five placebo) received 30 mg BID for 12 weeks. All participants were on nucleos(t)ide analog monotherapy for more than 6 months, with HBsAg between 100 and 1500 IU/mL, and serum ALT below 1× ULN. RESULTS: At Day 28, HBsAg reductions were -0.65 log10 IU/mL in the 30 mg BID 28-day group and -0.53 log10 IU/mL in the 60 mg BID 28-day group. The 30 mg BID 12-week group showed a greater reduction of -0.89 log10 IU/mL at the end of treatment versus placebo (p 50% reduction in HBsAg with a maximum decrease of 1.64 log10 IU/mL. Notably, 76.5% of patients in the 12-week group achieved HBsAg below 100 IU/mL. Rebounds in HBsAg were observed following treatment discontinuation. GST-HG131 was well tolerated, with no dose-related toxicity or emerging safety concerns across all cohorts. CONCLUSION: GST-HG131, a first-in-class oral PAPD5/7 inhibitor, demonstrated favourable safety and significant HBsAg reduction in patients with CHB. The greatest antiviral activity was observed after 12 weeks of treatment, supporting further clinical development of GST-HG131 as a component of functional cure strategies for CHB. source_records.title: Safety, Tolerability and Antiviral Activity of GST-HG131 in Chronic Hepatitis B: A Randomized, Double-Blind Phase IIa Study.
source_records.abstract: Background and aims Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains a major global health burden. Current therapies rarely achieve a functional cure due to low rates of HBsAg clearance, the persistence of the viral replication template-covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA)-and the need for lifelong treatment. GST-HG131 is a first-in-class, orally bioavailable small-molecule inhibitor of PAPD5/7, key host factors involved in HBV mRNA stabilization and HBsAg production. We evaluated the safety, tolerability and antiviral activity of GST-HG131 in patients with CHB receiving nucleos(t)ide analogue (NUC) therapy in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase IIa study. Methods This double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled Phase IIa study evaluated the efficacy and safety of GST-HG131 in 45 CHB patients. Cohorts 1 and 2 (n = 10 each; 8 active, 2 placebo) received 30 mg or 60 mg BID for 28 days, respectively. Cohort 3 (n = 25; 20 active, five placebo) received 30 mg BID for 12 weeks. All participants were on nucleos(t)ide analog monotherapy for more than 6 months, with HBsAg between 100 and 1500 IU/mL, and serum ALT below 1× ULN. Results At Day 28, HBsAg reductions were -0.65 log 10 IU/mL in the 30 mg BID 28-day group and -0.53 log 10 IU/mL in the 60 mg BID 28-day group. The 30 mg BID 12-week group showed a greater reduction of -0.89 log 10 IU/mL at the end of treatment versus placebo (p 50% reduction in HBsAg with a maximum decrease of 1.64 log 10 IU/mL. Notably, 76.5% of patients in the 12-week group achieved HBsAg below 100 IU/mL. Rebounds in HBsAg were observed following treatment discontinuation. GST-HG131 was well tolerated, with no dose-related toxicity or emerging safety concerns across all cohorts. Conclusion GST-HG131, a first-in-class oral PAPD5/7 inhibitor, demonstrated favourable safety and significant HBsAg reduction in patients with CHB. The greatest antiviral activity was observed after 12 weeks of treatment, supporting further clinical development of GST-HG131 as a component of functional cure strategies for CHB. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06263959.

analysis_zh.main_results: 在第28天时,30 mg每日两次28天组的HBsAg水平降低了-0.65 log10 IU/mL,而60 mg每日两次28天组的HBsAg水平降低了-0.53 log10 IU/mL。在治疗结束时,12周组的HBsAg水平比安慰剂组减少了更多的-0.89 log10 IU/mL。值得注意的是,12周组中有76.5%的患者实现了HBsAg低于100 IU/mL。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在12周的治疗后观察到最大的功能性治愈活性,支持进一步开展GST-HG131在慢性乙型肝炎功能性治愈策略中的临床开发。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,GST-HG131可能是一种有前景的候选药物,有助于改善慢性乙型肝炎患者中HBsAg的清除,从而可能为功能性治愈策略做出贡献。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究样本量较小且治疗时间较短,这可能影响其结果的普遍性。由于研究设计和有限的随访时间,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Finite Versus Indefinite Nucleos(t)ide Analogue Therapy in HBeAg‐Negative Chronic Hepatitis B: Meta‐Analysis of Randomized Trials.
papers.abstract: Continuous nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA) therapy for chronic hepatitis B (CHB) effectively maintains viral suppression but rarely results in functional cure. Finite NA therapy has been proposed to increase rates of HBsAg loss; however, international guidelines provide conflicting recommendations. This study compares the efficacy and safety of finite versus continuous NA therapy in HBeAg-negative adults using randomized controlled trials. We included parallel-group randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA) cessation versus continuation in non-cirrhotic, virally suppressed HBeAg-negative adults. Two reviewers independently screened studies and assessed risk of bias using Cochrane RoB 2. Random-effects Mantel-Haenszel meta-analyses with Hartung-Knapp adjustment and Paule-Mandel estimation were used to pool risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Certainty of evidence was assessed using the GRADE approach. Four RCTs (n = 357) met inclusion criteria. Discontinuation increased HBsAg loss vs. continuation (RR 5.02, 95% CI: 0.47-53.47; I 2 = 21.8%; low certainty), corresponding to ~53 additional losses per 1000 patients. However, finite therapy markedly increased virologic relapse (RR 23.09) and retreatment (RR 21.94) while reducing sustained off-therapy virologic response (RR 0.46). Post-cessation ALT flares were frequent but self-limited or resolved with retreatment. No hepatic decompensation or serious adverse events occurred. In monitored, non-cirrhotic adults, finite NA therapy may increase the probability of HBsAg loss despite predictable relapse and retreatment. With no evidence of severe harm, these findings support finite therapy as a selective, patient-centered strategy toward functional cure in expert centers.

papers.title: Projected Effect of 2026 Federal Changes to the Childhood Immunization Schedule on Chronic Hepatitis B Virus Infections in the United States.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The United States recently proposed changes to the recommendations for childhood hepatitis B virus (HBV) vaccination. OBJECTIVE: To project the effect of vaccine policy changes, if fully implemented, on chronic HBV infections. DESIGN: Markov cohort state transition model of perinatal and childhood HBV infection. DATA SOURCES: Published data on maternal HBV prevalence (0.4%) and hepatitis B surface antigen testing (99.5% sensitivity), childhood vaccine completion (universal birth-dose strategy: 91.1%; deferred strategy: 87.1%; shared decision-making strategy: 50.0%), and age-stratified risk for chronic HBV infection. TARGET POPULATION: One-year birth cohort of U.S.-born infants (n = 3.6 million). TIME HORIZON: 20 years. INTERVENTION: Universal birth-dose vaccination, deferred (2-month) vaccination, and vaccination through shared decision making. OUTCOME MEASURES: Numbers with chronic HBV infection and susceptibility to HBV, with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs) derived from probabilistic sensitivity analysis. RESULTS OF BASE-CASE ANALYSIS: Compared with the universal birth-dose strategy (255 childhood infections [95% UI, 130 to 530]), the deferred and shared decision-making strategies would increase chronic HBV infections in the 2026 birth cohort by 19% to 303 (95% UI, 155 to 610) and by 83% to 467 (95% UI, 209 to 1032), respectively. These strategies would also increase the number of HBV-susceptible people at year 20 (474 000 and 1 806 000) compared with the universal birth-dose strategy (232 000). RESULTS OF SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS: In a scenario with lower vaccine coverage (84.5%) and higher HBV prevalence (maternal prevalence of 0.72% and higher risk for horizontal infection), chronic HBV infections would increase to 1700 and 2192, respectively, with the deferred and shared decision-making strategies. LIMITATION: Uncertainty in horizontal HBV infection risk. CONCLUSION: Proposed policy changes for vaccination through shared decision making are projected to result in an 83% increase in childhood HBV infections, and between 50% and 70% of children entering adulthood annually would be susceptible to HBV infection. Policymakers should reimplement recommendations for universal birth-dose vaccination. PRIMARY FUNDING SOURCE: National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the potential impact of proposed changes to the U.S. childhood hepatitis B virus (HBV) vaccination schedule on chronic HBV infections. Using a Markov cohort state transition model, the researchers projected outcomes for a one-year birth cohort of 3.6 million U.S.-born infants over a 20-year time horizon. The analysis compared three vaccination strategies: universal birth-dose, deferred (2-month), and shared decision-making. Results indicated that the deferred and shared decision-making strategies would increase chronic HBV infections by 19% and 83%, respectively, compared to the universal birth-dose strategy. Additionally, these strategies would lead to higher numbers of HBV-susceptible individuals at year 20. The study highlights the importance of maintaining universal birth-dose vaccination to prevent chronic HBV infections and emphasizes the need for policymakers to consider these projections when revising immunization guidelines. However, the findings are limited by uncertainty in horizontal HBV infection risk, which affects the reliability of the projections.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 美国最近提出了对儿童乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)疫苗接种接种建议的调整。为了预测如果完全实施疫苗政策调整,对慢性HBV感染的影响。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 一种马尔可夫乙型肝炎病毒母婴传播和儿童感染状态转移模型被采用。目标人群为美国出生婴儿的一岁出生(n = 3.6百万)。时间范围为20年。
elements_zh.methods: 数据来源:发表的关于母亲HBV 患病率(0.4%)和乙肝表面抗原检测(99.5%灵敏度)的数据,儿童疫苗接种完成率(普遍出生剂量策略:91.1%;延迟策略:87.1%;共享决策策略:50.0%),以及按年龄分层的慢性HBV感染风险。
elements_zh.main_results: 基线分析结果:与普遍接种出生剂量策略(255例儿童感染 [95% 置信区间,130至530])相比,延迟接种和共享决策策略将使2026年出生的队列研究地区的慢性HBV感染人数分别增加19%至303(95% 置信区间,155至610)和83%至467(95% 置信区间,209至1032)。这些策略还将使20年后的HBV易感人群数量分别增加至474 000和1 806 000,相比普遍接种出生剂量策略的232 000。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 通过共享决策进行的疫苗接种接种政策调整预计会导致儿童HBV感染增加83%,并且每年有50%至70%的儿童进入成年时仍对HBV感染易感。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,疫苗接种接种政策的调整可能显著影响美国人群中慢性HBV感染的患病率和HBV感染的易感性,为未来的公共卫生策略和疫苗接种建议提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 水平HBV传播风险的不确定性限制了预测的可信度。证据强度为中等,因为其依赖于已发表的数据和概率敏感性分析。

papers.title: Long-term temporal trends in hepatitis B and C among blood donors in Brazil: Prevalence, incidence, and demographic correlates from the REDS multicenter program.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Viral hepatitis remains a major public health challenge. We evaluated long-term trends in hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) prevalence, incidence, and force of infection (FOI) among blood donors from five Brazilian blood centers and investigated associated demographic factors. STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: Data from the NHLBI Recipient Epidemiology and Donor Evaluation Study program were analyzed. Prevalence was estimated among 2,062,816 first-time donors for HBV (2008-2023) and 1,673,745 for HCV (2012-2023). Incidence was estimated among 1,346,256 repeat donors for HBV and 1,151,209 for HCV. Active HBV infection was defined by reactive HBsAg and anti-HBc or reactive HBV nucleic acid testing (NAT), and active HCV infection by reactive NAT. Historical FOI was estimated using a Bayesian serocatalytic model. RESULTS: Active infection prevalence was 136.2 per 100,000 donors (95% CI, 131.2-141.3) for HBV and 57.4 (95% CI, 53.8-61.1) for HCV. Incidence rates were 3.54 (95% CI, 3.01-4.11) and 3.99 (95% CI, 3.33-4.72) per 100,000 person-years, respectively. Prevalence decreased annually by 7.6% for HBV and 11.0% for HCV. Higher prevalence and incidence were associated with male sex, older age, lower educational attainment, and Black or mixed-race skin color. Regional differences persisted, and FOI declined markedly for both infections. DISCUSSION: HBV and HCV prevalence, incidence, and FOI declined substantially among Brazilian blood donors, suggesting reduced transmission, although improved donor selection and screening may also have contributed. Persistent demographic and regional disparities support continued surveillance and targeted prevention.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed long-term trends in hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) prevalence, incidence, and force of infection among blood donors in Brazil from 2008 to 2023. It found that HBV and HCV prevalence and incidence decreased over time, with HBV prevalence dropping by 7.6% annually and HCV by 11.0%. The decline was associated with demographic factors such as male sex, older age, lower educational attainment, and Black or mixed-race skin color. Regional disparities persisted, and the force of infection for both viruses declined significantly. The authors suggest that reduced transmission may be due to improved donor selection and screening. These findings highlight the importance of continued surveillance and targeted prevention strategies to address persistent disparities in HBV and HCV infection rates among blood donors in Brazil.

papers.title: Abstract C042: Awareness of hepatitis B and hepatitis C viruses as causes of cancer among U.S. adults: Findings from HINTS 7
papers.abstract: Abstract Background: Chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) and hepatitis B virus (HBV) infections are major causes of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet public awareness that these infections can cause cancer remains poorly characterized. We examined sociodemographic predictors of awareness that HCV and HBV can cause cancer among U.S. Methods: Data were analyzed from the 2024 Health Information National Trends Survey (HINTS 7), a nationally representative survey of U.S. Two separate survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression models assessed factors associated with correctly identifying HCV and HBV as causes of cancer. Analyses incorporated jackknife replicate weights and adjusted for age, sex, race/ethnicity, education, household income, rurality, Appalachian residence, health insurance status, self-rated health, and cancer history. Complete-case analysis was used for each model. Results: The sample included 7,278 U.S. After weighting, 50.8% were male, 48.4% were female, 60.6% were non-Hispanic White, 87.0% resided in urban areas, and 91.4% had health insurance. Approximately 16.7% correctly identified HCV as a cause of cancer, and 18.0% correctly identified HBV as a cause of cancer. Rurality, Appalachian residence, sex, race/ethnicity, insurance status, and cancer history were not independently associated with awareness. Conclusions: Awareness that HCV and HBV can cause cancer was low nationally, with fewer than one in five U.S. adults correctly identifying these associations. Lower educational attainment and older age were associated with lower awareness, highlighting priority populations for HCC prevention and viral hepatitis education efforts. Citation Format: Rachel A. Awareness of hepatitis B and hepatitis C viruses as causes of cancer among U.S. adults: Findings from HINTS 7 [abstract]. In: Proceedings of the 19th AACR Conference on the Science of Cancer Health Disparities; 2026 Oct 18-21; Atlanta, GA. Philadelphia (PA): AACR; Cancer Epidemiol Biomarkers Prev 2026;35(10 Suppl):Abstract nr C042.

analysis.methods: Two separate survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression models assessed factors associated with correctly identifying HCV and HBV as causes of cancer. Analyses incorporated jackknife replicate weights and adjusted for age, sex, race/ethnicity, education, household income, rurality, Appalachian residence, health insurance status, self-rated health, and cancer history. Complete-case analysis was used for each model.
analysis.main_results: The sample included 7,278 U.S. After weighting, 50.8% were male, 48.4% were female, 60.6% were non-Hispanic White, 87.0% resided in urban areas, and 91.4% had health insurance. Approximately 16.7% correctly identified HCV as a cause of cancer, and 18.0% correctly identified HBV as a cause of cancer. Rurality, Appalachian residence, sex, race/ethnicity, insurance status, and cancer history were not independently associated with awareness.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Lower educational attainment and older age were associated with lower awareness, highlighting priority populations for HCC prevention and viral hepatitis education efforts.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings underscore the need for targeted education efforts to improve awareness of HBV and HCV as causes of cancer, particularly among populations with lower educational attainment and older age groups.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on self-reported data and the use of complete-case analysis, which may introduce bias. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to assess public awareness of hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) as causes of cancer among U.S. adults. Using data from the 2024 Health Information National Trends Survey (HINTS 7), a nationally representative survey, the researchers conducted two multivariable logistic regression models to evaluate sociodemographic predictors of awareness. The results showed that approximately 16.7% of adults correctly identified HCV as a cause of cancer, and 18.0% correctly identified HBV as a cause of cancer. Lower educational attainment and older age were associated with lower awareness. The study highlights the need for targeted education efforts to improve awareness of HBV and HCV as cancer-causing agents, particularly among vulnerable populations. However, the study has limitations, including reliance on self-reported data and the use of complete-case analysis, which may affect the strength of the evidence.

papers.title_zh: 摘要 C042:美国成年人对乙型肝炎病毒和丙型肝炎病毒作为癌症病因的认知:来自HINTS 7的研究结果
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background: Chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) and hepatitis B virus (HBV) infections are major causes of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet public awareness that these infections can cause cancer remains poorly characterized. We examined sociodemographic predictors of awareness that HCV and HBV can cause cancer among U.S. Methods: Data were analyzed from the 2024 Health Information National Trends Survey (HINTS 7), a nationally representative survey of U.S. Two separate survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression models assessed factors associated with correctly identifying HCV and HBV as causes of cancer. Analyses incorporated jackknife replicate weights and adjusted for age, sex, race/ethnicity, education, household income, rurality, Appalachian residence, health insurance status, self-rated health, and cancer history. Complete-case analysis was used for each model. Results: The sample included 7,278 U.S. After weighting, 50.8% were male, 48.4% were female, 60.6% were non-Hispanic White, 87.0% resided in urban areas, and 91.4% had health insurance. Approximately 16.7% correctly identified HCV as a cause of cancer, and 18.0% correctly identified HBV as a cause of cancer. Rurality, Appalachian residence, sex, race/ethnicity, insurance status, and cancer history were not independently associated with awareness. Conclusions: Awareness that HCV and HBV can cause cancer was low nationally, with fewer than one in five U.S. adults correctly identifying these associations. Lower educational attainment and older age were associated with lower awareness, highlighting priority populations for HCC prevention and viral hepatitis education efforts. Citation Format: Rachel A. Awareness of hepatitis B and hepatitis C viruses as causes of cancer among U.S. adults: Findings from HINTS 7 [abstract]. In: Proceedings of the 19th AACR Conference on the Science of Cancer Health Disparities; 2026 Oct 18-21; Atlanta, GA. Philadelphia (PA): AACR; Cancer Epidemiol Biomarkers Prev 2026;35(10 Suppl):Abstract nr C042.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景:慢性丙型肝炎病毒(HCV)和乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)感染是肝细胞癌(HCC)的主要病因,但公众对这些感染可能导致癌症的认知仍不明确。我们研究了美国成年人中对HCV和HBV作为癌症病因的认知的社会人口学预测因素。方法:数据来源于2024年健康信息国家趋势调查(HINTS 7),这是美国全国代表性调查。两个独立的加权多变量逻辑回归模型评估了正确识别HCV和HBV作为癌症病因的因素。分析采用了jackknife复制权重,并调整了年龄、性别、种族/民族、教育程度、家庭收入、农村地区居住、阿巴拉契亚地区居住、健康保险状况、自我评价健康状况和癌症史。每个模型均采用完整案例分析。结果:样本包括7,278名美国成年人。加权后,50.8%为男性,48.4%为女性,60.6%为非西班牙裔白人,87.0%居住在城市地区,91.4%拥有健康保险。约16.7%正确识别HCV为癌症病因,18.0%正确识别HBV为癌症病因。农村地区居住、阿巴拉契亚地区居住、性别、种族/民族、保险状况和癌症史均未独立与认知相关。结论:全国范围内对HCV和HBV作为癌症病因的认知较低,不到五分之一的美国成年人正确识别这些关联。较低的教育水平和较大的年龄与较低的认知相关,突显了HCC预防和病毒性肝炎教育的重点人群。引用格式:Rachel A. 美国成年人对乙型肝炎病毒和丙型肝炎病毒作为癌症病因的认知:来自HINTS 7的研究结果 [摘要]。载于:第19届AACR癌症健康差异科学会议论文集;2026年10月18-21日;佐治亚州亚特兰大。费城(PA):AACR;Cancer Epidemiol Biomarkers Prev 2026;35(10 Suppl):摘要编号C042。

papers.title: Passive acquisition of hepatitis B virus antibodies after allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Newly positive hepatitis B virus (HBV) serologic results after allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) may reflect passive antibody transfer from blood-derived products rather than HBV infection. We investigated the incidence and temporal patterns of hepatitis B surface antibody (anti-HBs) and antibody to hepatitis B core antibody (anti-HBc) acquisition after allogeneic HCT. STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated 193 adults who underwent allogeneic HCT for hematologic diseases between May 2012 and March 2025 at a single institution in Japan. Anti-HBs, anti-HBc, and hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) were assessed before and after HCT. RESULTS: Among 180 patients who were anti-HBc negative before HCT, 6 (3.3%) developed anti-HBc positivity after HCT. Among 164 patients who were anti-HBs negative before HCT, 49 (29.9%) developed anti-HBs positivity. All patients with newly detectable antibodies remained HBsAg negative, and available HBV DNA measurements showed no evidence of active HBV infection. Among patients with subsequent follow-up measurements, anti-HBc disappeared in 3 of 3 evaluable patients after a median of 240 days, whereas anti-HBs declined or disappeared in 30 of 32 evaluable patients after a median of 119 days. Among patients receiving neither fresh frozen plasma nor intravenous immunoglobulin, anti-HBs concentrations increased significantly after HCT (p< .0001), with a greater increase among those receiving ≥24 versus ≤23 platelet transfusions (p = .0437). DISCUSSION: Newly detectable HBV antibodies were common after HCT without virologic evidence of infection, suggesting passive antibody transfer from cellular blood components, particularly platelets.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Newly positive hepatitis B virus (HBV) serologic results after allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) may reflect passive antibody transfer from blood-derived products rather than HBV infection.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We investigated the incidence and temporal patterns of hepatitis B surface antibody (anti-HBs) and antibody to hepatitis B core antibody (anti-HBc) acquisition after allogeneic HCT in 193 adults who underwent the procedure for hematologic diseases between May 2012 and March 2025 at a single institution in Japan.
analysis.methods: Anti-HBs, anti-HBc, and hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) were assessed before and after HCT, with follow-up measurements to evaluate antibody persistence.
analysis.main_results: Among 180 patients who were anti-HBc negative before HCT, 6 (3.3%) developed anti-HBc positivity after HCT. Among 164 patients who were anti-HBs negative before HCT, 49 (29.9%) developed anti-HBs positivity. All patients with newly detectable antibodies remained HBsAg negative, and available HBV DNA measurements showed no evidence of active HBV infection. Among patients with subsequent follow-up measurements, anti-HBc disappeared in 3 of 3 evaluable patients after a median of 240 days, whereas anti-HBs declined or disappeared in 30 of 32 evaluable patients after a median of 119 days.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Newly detectable HBV antibodies were common after HCT without virologic evidence of infection, suggesting passive antibody transfer from cellular blood components, particularly platelets.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings highlight the importance of distinguishing between passive antibody transfer and active HBV infection in post-transplant patients, which has implications for accurate diagnosis and monitoring of HBV status.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is retrospective and based on a single institution in Japan, which may limit generalizability. The evidence is moderate due to the reliance on serologic data without direct virologic confirmation in all cases.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the incidence and temporal patterns of hepatitis B surface antibody (anti-HBs) and antibody to hepatitis B core antibody (anti-HBc) acquisition after allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) in patients with no prior evidence of HBV infection. The research highlights that newly detectable HBV antibodies may result from passive transfer from blood-derived products rather than active infection. Among 180 patients who were anti-HBc negative before HCT, 6 (3.3%) developed anti-HBc positivity, while 49 (29.9%) of 164 anti-HBs negative patients became positive. All patients with newly detectable antibodies remained HBsAg negative, and HBV DNA measurements showed no evidence of active infection. Follow-up data indicated that anti-HBc disappeared in 3 of 3 evaluable patients after a median of 240 days, whereas anti-HBs declined or disappeared in 30 of 32 evaluable patients after a median of 119 days. The authors suggest that these findings indicate passive antibody transfer from cellular blood components, particularly platelets, rather than HBV infection. The study's implications emphasize the need for careful interpretation of serologic results in post-transplant patients to avoid misdiagnosis.

papers.title_zh: 异基因造血细胞移植后乙型肝炎病毒抗体的被动获得
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Newly positive hepatitis B virus (HBV) serologic results after allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) may reflect passive antibody transfer from blood-derived products rather than HBV infection. We investigated the incidence and temporal patterns of hepatitis B surface antibody (anti-HBs) and antibody to hepatitis B core antibody (anti-HBc) acquisition after allogeneic HCT. STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated 193 adults who underwent allogeneic HCT for hematologic diseases between May 2012 and March 2025 at a single institution in Japan. Anti-HBs, anti-HBc, and hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) were assessed before and after HCT. RESULTS: Among 180 patients who were anti-HBc negative before HCT, 6 (3.3%) developed anti-HBc positivity after HCT. Among 164 patients who were anti-HBs negative before HCT, 49 (29.9%) developed anti-HBs positivity. All patients with newly detectable antibodies remained HBsAg negative, and available HBV DNA measurements showed no evidence of active HBV infection. Among patients with subsequent follow-up measurements, anti-HBc disappeared in 3 of 3 evaluable patients after a median of 240 days, whereas anti-HBs declined or disappeared in 30 of 32 evaluable patients after a median of 119 days. Among patients receiving neither fresh frozen plasma nor intravenous immunoglobulin, anti-HBs concentrations increased significantly after HCT (p< .0001), with a greater increase among those receiving ≥24 versus ≤23 platelet transfusions (p = .0437). DISCUSSION: Newly detectable HBV antibodies were common after HCT without virologic evidence of infection, suggesting passive antibody transfer from cellular blood components, particularly platelets.

papers.title: Hepatitis B surface antigen-targeting strategies for clearance: A review of progress from mechanistic exploration to clinical translation
papers.abstract: Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) persistence hinders the achievement of a functional cure in patients with chronic hepatitis B. Strategies to suppress or eliminate HBsAg and break the host immune tolerance while restoring immune response become key components of immune therapy-directed clinical cure.Agents that target HBsAg include monoclonal antibodies, small interfering RNAs, antisense oligonucleotides, gene editing technologies, capsid assembly modulators, and therapeutic agents targeting secretion pathways.Immune checkpoint inhibitors and other immune-based clearance approaches are also included within this strategic framework.These agents target the HBsAg lifecycle and its source templates, including covalently closed circular DNA and integrated hepatitis B virus DNA in the host genome.This article reviews these strategies by synthesizing the latest information from preclinical studies and clinical trials, summarises their mechanism and efficacy, discusses challenges and prospects for combinations, and aims to provide a scientific basis for chronic hepatitis B curative research.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on strategies to clear Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) in patients with chronic hepatitis B, aiming to achieve a functional cure by suppressing or eliminating HBsAg and breaking host immune tolerance while restoring immune response.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review synthesizes the latest information from preclinical studies and clinical trials, summarizing the mechanisms and efficacy of various agents targeting HBsAg, including monoclonal antibodies, small interfering RNAs, antisense oligonucleotides, gene editing technologies, capsid assembly modulators, and therapeutic agents targeting secretion pathways. It also includes immune checkpoint inhibitors and other immune-based clearance approaches.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review highlights that targeting HBsAg lifecycle and its source templates, such as covalently closed circular DNA and integrated hepatitis B virus DNA in the host genome, is a key component of immune therapy-directed clinical cure. analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies heterogeneity in the efficacy of different agents and challenges in combining strategies. It also notes the need for further research to address unresolved mechanisms and improve the outcomes of immune-based clearance approaches.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests specific priorities for research, including the development of more effective agents targeting HBsAg and its source templates, as well as the exploration of combination therapies to enhance immune response and achieve a functional cure.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores strategies for clearing Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) in patients with chronic hepatitis B, emphasizing the importance of targeting HBsAg lifecycle and its source templates, such as covalently closed circular DNA and integrated hepatitis B virus DNA. It synthesizes preclinical and clinical data on various agents, including monoclonal antibodies, small interfering RNAs, and immune checkpoint inhibitors, and discusses their mechanisms, efficacy, and challenges. The review highlights the need for further research to address heterogeneity in treatment responses and to develop more effective combination therapies. These findings provide a scientific basis for advancing curative research in chronic hepatitis B.

elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 综述强调,靶向HBsAg生命周期及其来源模板,如共价闭合环状DNA(共价闭合环状DNA)和整合在宿主基因组中的乙型肝炎病毒DNA,是免疫治疗导向临床治愈的关键组成部分。它讨论了这些策略组合的挑战与前景。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 综述指出不同药物在疗效上的异质性以及策略组合的挑战。它还提到需要进一步研究以解决未明确的机制并改善基于免疫的清除方法的疗效。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 综述建议了具体的研究优先事项,包括开发更有效的针对HBsAg及其来源模板的药物,以及探索组合疗法以增强免疫应答并实现功能性治愈。

papers.abstract_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒表面抗原(HBsAg)的持续存在阻碍了慢性乙型肝炎患者的功能性治愈。抑制或清除HBsAg并打破免疫耐受、恢复免疫应答的策略成为免疫治疗导向临床治愈的关键组成部分。针对HBsAg的药物包括单克隆抗体、小干扰RNA、反义寡核苷酸、基因编辑技术、衣壳组装调节剂以及靶向分泌途径的治疗药物。免疫检查点抑制剂和其他基于免疫的清除方法也包含在这一战略框架中。这些药物靶向HBsAg生命周期及其来源模板,包括共价闭合环状DNA(共价闭合环状DNA)和整合在宿主基因组中的乙型肝炎病毒DNA。本文通过综合预临床研究和临床试验的最新信息,回顾了这些策略,总结了其机制和疗效,讨论了组合策略的挑战与前景,并旨在为功能性治愈研究提供科学依据。

papers.title: Distinct immune signatures define hepatitis D- versus hepatitis B-associated hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Hepatitis D is the most severe form of viral hepatitis. However, the clinical, virological, and systemic inflammatory characteristics of HDV-associated HCC remain insufficiently characterized. METHODS: In this single-center retrospective study, we identified 162 patients with HCC due to chronic hepatitis D (HDV-HCC; n=54) or chronic hepatitis B (HBV-HCC; n=108). Plasma levels of 92 soluble inflammatory mediators (SIMs) were quantified using proximity extension assay in HCC patients [HBV-HCC (n=50), HDV-HCC (n=30), and matched non-HCC controls (HBV=19, HDV=17)]. RESULTS: At the time of HCC diagnosis, patients with CHD were younger, had more impaired liver synthesis and detoxification function, and lower levels of AST, CRP, and leukocytes. HDV-HCCs presented with smaller tumors, less frequent portal vein infiltration, and more often fulfilled Milan criteria (all p<0.01). Systemic immune profiling revealed distinct inflammatory patterns between both etiologies. Compared with HBV-HCC, HDV-HCC was characterized by a comparatively stronger IL-10-associated immunoregulatory signature, whereas HBV-HCC exhibited a more pronounced pro-inflammatory profile involving IL-6- and phosphorylation- and proliferation-associated signaling. Despite these differences, event-free survival did not differ between groups. CONCLUSIONS: HBV-HCC more frequently presented with advanced tumor stage, whereas HDV-HCC was associated with more severe underlying liver disease but smaller tumors. Importantly, HBV-associated and HDV-associated HCC exhibit distinct systemic inflammatory signatures, potentially reflecting differences in systemic immune regulation between etiologies. These findings may have implications for biomarker development and future etiology-specific therapeutic strategies.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to characterize the distinct immune signatures of hepatitis D- versus hepatitis B-associated hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) to address the insufficient understanding of HDV-associated HCC.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A single-center retrospective study included 162 patients with HCC, 54 with chronic hepatitis D (HDV-HCC) and 108 with chronic hepatitis B (HBV-HCC).
analysis.methods: Plasma levels of 92 soluble inflammatory mediators were quantified using proximity extension assay in HCC patients, including 50 HBV-HCC, 30 HDV-HCC, and matched non-HCC controls.
analysis.main_results: HDV-HCC patients were younger, had more impaired liver function, and lower levels of AST, CRP, and leukocytes. HDV-HCC tumors were smaller, less frequently infiltrated, and more often fulfilled Milan criteria. Systemic immune profiling revealed distinct inflammatory patterns between HDV-HCC and HBV-HCC.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: HDV-HCC was characterized by a stronger IL-10-associated immunoregulatory signature, while HBV-HCC exhibited a more pronounced pro-inflammatory profile. These findings suggest differences in systemic immune regulation between the two etiologies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The distinct systemic inflammatory signatures of HDV-HCC and HBV-HCC may have implications for biomarker development and etiology-specific therapeutic strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its single-center design and retrospective nature, which may affect generalizability. The sample size for HDV-HCC is relatively small, and the lack of randomization may introduce bias.

analysis.summary_en: This study compared immune signatures in HDV-HCC and HBV-HCC, revealing distinct inflammatory patterns and suggesting differences in systemic immune regulation between the two etiologies, with implications for biomarker development and therapeutic strategies.

papers.title_zh: 不同的免疫特征定义了与乙型肝炎病毒相关和与丁型肝炎病毒相关的肝细胞癌。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Hepatitis D is the most severe form of viral hepatitis. However, the clinical, virological, and systemic inflammatory characteristics of HDV-associated HCC remain insufficiently characterized. METHODS: In this single-center retrospective study, we identified 162 patients with HCC due to chronic hepatitis D (HDV-HCC; n=54) or chronic hepatitis B (HBV-HCC; n=108). Plasma levels of 92 soluble inflammatory mediators (SIMs) were quantified using proximity extension assay in HCC patients [HBV-HCC (n=50), HDV-HCC (n=30), and matched non-HCC controls (HBV=19, HDV=17)]. RESULTS: At the time of HCC diagnosis, patients with CHD were younger, had more impaired liver synthesis and detoxification function, and lower levels of AST, CRP, and leukocytes. HDV-HCCs presented with smaller tumors, less frequent portal vein infiltration, and more often fulfilled Milan criteria (all p<0.01). Systemic immune profiling revealed distinct inflammatory patterns between both etiologies. Compared with HBV-HCC, HDV-HCC was characterized by a comparatively stronger IL-10-associated immunoregulatory signature, whereas HBV-HCC exhibited a more pronounced pro-inflammatory profile involving IL-6- and phosphorylation- and proliferation-associated signaling. Despite these differences, event-free survival did not differ between groups. CONCLUSIONS: HBV-HCC more frequently presented with advanced tumor stage, whereas HDV-HCC was associated with more severe underlying liver disease but smaller tumors. Importantly, HBV-associated and HDV-associated HCC exhibit distinct systemic inflammatory signatures, potentially reflecting differences in systemic immune regulation between etiologies. These findings may have implications for biomarker development and future etiology-specific therapeutic strategies.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:肝细胞癌(HCC)是全球癌症相关死亡的主要原因之一。丁型肝炎病毒(HDV)是病毒性肝炎中最严重的形式。然而,与HDV相关的HCC的临床、病毒学和全身炎症特征仍不够明确。方法:本研究为单中心回顾性研究,纳入了162例因慢性乙型肝炎(HBV-HCC;n=108)或慢性丁型肝炎(HDV-HCC;n=54)导致的HCC患者。使用邻近扩展检测法(proximity extension assay)对HCC患者的血浆中92种可溶性炎症介质(SIMs)水平进行了定量分析,包括50例HBV-HCC、30例HDV-HCC以及匹配的非HCC对照组(HBV=19,HDV=17)。结果:在HCC诊断时,慢性乙型肝炎患者年龄较小,肝合成和解毒功能受损更严重,AST、CRP和白细胞水平较低。HDV-HCC肿瘤体积较小,门静脉浸润较少见,且更常符合米兰标准(所有p<0.01)。全身免疫特征分析显示两种病因的HCC具有不同的炎症模式。与HBV-HCC相比,HDV-HCC表现出更强的IL-10相关免疫调节特征,而HBV-HCC则表现出更显著的促炎特征,涉及IL-6和磷酸化及增殖相关信号。尽管存在这些差异,各组的无事件生存率没有显著差异。结论:HBV-HCC更常表现为晚期肿瘤阶段,而HDV-HCC则与更严重的潜在肝病但较小的肿瘤相关。重要的是,HBV相关和HDV相关的HCC表现出不同的全身炎症特征,这可能反映了两种病因之间系统性免疫调节的差异。这些发现可能对生物标志物的开发和未来针对病因的治疗策略具有重要意义。

papers.title: Comprehensive Prevention and Control Service Capacity for Hepatitis B in Medical and Health Institutions: A Cross-Sectional Survey in Jiangsu Province, China
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Despite substantial progress in hepatitis B virus (HBV) prevention in China, important gaps remain in diagnosis, referral, treatment, and long-term follow-up. To further strengthen viral hepatitis prevention and control, the National Administration of Disease Control and Prevention formulated the Action Plan for the Prevention and Control of Viral Hepatitis in China (2025–2030) in 2025. Jiangsu Province is classified as a region with moderate endemicity of HBV in China. The capacity of medical and health institutions to deliver comprehensive HBV prevention and control services is essential for effective implementation of HBV control strategies. This study aimed to assess the capacity of medical and health institutions in Jiangsu Province across key components of the HBV prevention and control service chain, including testing, diagnosis reporting, referral, antiviral treatment and follow-up management. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted across all 13 prefecture-level cities in Jiangsu Province, encompassing 183 medical and health institutions—comprising 135 hospitals and 48 disease control and prevention centers (CDCs). The survey encompassed the following core items: Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) testing, HBV-DNA testing, case diagnosis, case referral, antiviral treatment, patient follow-up, and public health prevention and control initiatives implemented by CDCs. Results Among the 183 surveyed institutions, 86.9% (159/183) reported having the capacity to perform HBsAg testing. In 2025, a total of 3.75 million HBsAg tests had been completed, over 90% of which were carried out in tertiary hospitals. HBV-DNA testing was available in 56.8% (104/183) of the surveyed institutions, and all primary hospitals offering this service outsource testing to independent clinical laboratories. Case referral services were provided by 37.2% (68/183) of the institutions, with antiviral treatment resources highly concentrated in tertiary hospitals. Follow-up management was implemented in 34.1% (46/135) of hospitals, mainly among tertiary hospitals. Conclusion Medical and health institutions in Jiangsu Province have established relatively strong capacity for HBV laboratory testing, particularly for HBsAg testing. However, HBV treatment and follow-up services remain highly concentrated in tertiary hospitals, indicating limited participation of primary-level institutions in long-term HBV management. Future efforts should focus on strengthening the HBV prevention and control service chain by unifying clinical diagnostic criteria, enhancing referral mechanisms, expanding grassroots follow-up capacity, and promoting coordinated information sharing between healthcare institutions and CDCs.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估江苏省医疗和健康机构提供全面HBV预防与控制服务的能力,以弥补中国在HBV预防方面取得进展后,病例报告、转诊、病毒检测和随访管理方面的差距。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在江苏省的13个地级市开展了横断面调查,涵盖183家医疗和健康机构,包括135家医院和48家疾病预防控制中心。
elements_zh.methods: 调查评估了HBsAg检测、HBV-DNA检测、病例报告、转诊、病毒检测和随访管理,以及疾病预防控制中心(CDC)实施的公共卫生预防与控制措施。
elements_zh.main_results: 在被调查的183家机构中,86.9%报告具备进行HBsAg检测的能力,而HBV-DNA检测在56.8%的机构中可用,随访管理在34.1%的医院中实施,主要集中在三级医院。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究发现,尽管HBV实验室检测能力,尤其是HBsAg检测能力较强,但HBV病毒检测和随访服务仍高度集中在三级医院,表明基层机构在长期HBV管理中的参与度有限。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,未来需要加强HBV预防与控制服务链,统一临床诊断标准,增强转诊机制,扩大基层随访能力,并促进医疗机构与CDC之间的协调信息共享。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 调查依赖于自我报告数据,可能引入偏倚,且HBV病毒检测和随访服务在三级医院的高度集中限制了研究结果在基层机构中的普遍适用性。

papers.title: Realizing personalized prediction for the reversal of chronic hepatitis B-associated liver fibrosis through machine learning
papers.abstract: Although long-term antiviral therapy can reverse liver fibrosis in a considerable proportion of patients with chronic hepatitis B, treatment response differs markedly among individuals, and reliable methods for predicting who will benefit remain lacking. Conventional clinical tools such as liver stiffness measurement and the aspartate aminotransferase-to-platelet ratio index were originally dewsigned for cross-sectional staging rather than longitudinal prediction, and their ability to capture the dynamic process of fibrosis reversal is limited. In this opinion review, we discuss how machine learning (ML) may help address this unmet need. We focus on three areas where ML has shown early but encouraging results: Quantitative analysis of images using ML, integration of pathological and clinical data through multimodal models, and dynamic prediction of treatment response based on serial measurements during antiviral therapy. In our view, the greatest value of ML lies not in replacing existing assessment tools but in complementing them, particularly through the early identification of patients who are unlikely to achieve fibrosis reversal with antiviral therapy alone. However, we also caution that most current models have been developed from small, single-center retrospective cohorts, and their clinical adoption will require prospective multi-center validation, improved model interpretability, and adherence to standardized reporting frameworks.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the lack of reliable methods for predicting individual treatment response in chronic hepatitis B patients, as long-term antiviral therapy can reverse liver fibrosis in some individuals but not others.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This opinion review discusses the application of machine learning in predicting treatment response for chronic hepatitis B, focusing on the potential of ML to complement existing clinical tools.
analysis.methods: The authors review the use of machine learning in three areas: quantitative image analysis, integration of pathological and clinical data through multimodal models, and dynamic prediction of treatment response based on serial measurements during antiviral therapy.
analysis.main_results: The review highlights early but encouraging results from machine learning applications in predicting fibrosis reversal in chronic hepatitis B, particularly through the integration of clinical and pathological data.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that machine learning can enhance existing tools for assessing treatment response in chronic hepatitis B, offering a novel approach to personalized prediction without replacing current methods.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that machine learning could improve the precision of predicting which patients with chronic hepatitis B are likely to achieve fibrosis reversal, aiding in more tailored treatment strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited by the fact that most current models are based on small, single-center retrospective cohorts, which may affect their generalizability and require further prospective validation.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the potential of machine learning to address the challenge of predicting individual responses to antiviral therapy in chronic hepatitis B patients. The authors highlight three promising areas: image-based quantitative analysis, integration of clinical and pathological data through multimodal models, and dynamic prediction based on serial measurements. They emphasize that while ML shows early promise, its clinical adoption requires validation across larger, multi-center studies and improved model interpretability. The study underscores the importance of using ML to complement existing tools rather than replace them, offering a novel approach to personalized treatment strategies. However, the evidence is limited by the reliance on small, single-center datasets, which may restrict the generalizability of findings. The implications of this work suggest that ML could enhance the precision of predicting fibrosis reversal in chronic hepatitis B, contributing to more effective and individualized care.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the lack of reliable methods for predicting individual treatment response in chronic hepatitis B patients, as long-term antiviral therapy can reverse liver fibrosis in some individuals but not others.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: This opinion review discusses the application of machine learning in predicting treatment response for chronic hepatitis B, focusing on the potential of ML to complement existing clinical tools.
analysis_en.methods: The authors review the use of machine learning in three areas: quantitative image analysis, integration of pathological and clinical data through multimodal models, and dynamic prediction of treatment response based on serial measurements during antiviral therapy.
analysis_en.main_results: The review highlights early but encouraging results from machine learning applications in predicting fibrosis reversal in chronic hepatitis B, particularly through the integration of clinical and pathological data.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that machine learning can enhance existing tools for assessing treatment response in chronic hepatitis B, offering a novel approach to personalized prediction without replacing current methods.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that machine learning could improve the precision of predicting which patients with chronic hepatitis B are likely to achieve fibrosis reversal, aiding in more tailored treatment strategies.

papers.title_zh: 通过机器学习实现针对慢性乙型肝炎相关肝纤维化的个性化预测
papers.source_body_en: Although long-term antiviral therapy can reverse liver fibrosis in a considerable proportion of patients with chronic hepatitis B, treatment response differs markedly among individuals, and reliable methods for predicting who will benefit remain lacking. Conventional clinical tools such as liver stiffness measurement and the aspartate aminotransferase-to-platelet ratio index were originally dewsigned for cross-sectional staging rather than longitudinal prediction, and their ability to capture the dynamic process of fibrosis reversal is limited. In this opinion review, we discuss how machine learning (ML) may help address this unmet need. We focus on three areas where ML has shown early but encouraging results: Quantitative analysis of images using ML, integration of pathological and clinical data through multimodal models, and dynamic prediction of treatment response based on serial measurements during antiviral therapy. In our view, the greatest value of ML lies not in replacing existing assessment tools but in complementing them, particularly through the early identification of patients who are unlikely to achieve fibrosis reversal with antiviral therapy alone. However, we also caution that most current models have been developed from small, single-center retrospective cohorts, and their clinical adoption will require prospective multi-center validation, improved model interpretability, and adherence to standardized reporting frameworks.
papers.abstract_zh: 尽管长期抗病毒药物治疗可以逆转慢性乙型肝炎患者的肝纤维化,但个体对治疗的反应差异显著,目前仍缺乏可靠的预测方法。传统的临床工具如肝硬度测量和天门冬氨酸氨基转移酶与血小板比值指数最初设计用于横断面分期,而非纵向预测,其捕捉纤维化逆转动态过程的能力有限。在本观点综述中,我们讨论了机器学习(ML)如何帮助解决这一未满足的需求。我们重点关注了机器学习在三个方面的早期但有希望的结果:利用机器学习进行图像的定量分析、通过多模态模型整合病理和临床数据,以及基于抗病毒药物治疗期间的连续测量动态预测治疗反应。我们认为,机器学习的最大价值并不在于取代现有评估工具,而在于补充它们,特别是在早期识别那些仅通过抗病毒药物治疗难以实现纤维化逆转的患者方面。然而,我们也提醒,目前大多数模型都是基于小规模、单中心的回顾性队列研究开发的,其临床应用需要前瞻性多中心验证、提高模型的可解释性以及遵循标准化的报告框架。

papers.title: Patient-reported treatment burden, communication, and persistence intention during add-on peginterferon alfa-2b therapy for chronic hepatitis B: a cross-sectional study
papers.abstract: Background Add-on peginterferon alfa-2b (Peg-IFN) may help reduce hepatitis B surface antigen levels and achieve a functional cure in selected patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB), but the treatment burden can make a finite course difficult to complete. We examined the patient-reported factors associated with thoughts of discontinuation and intentions to persist with treatment during add-on Peg-IFN therapy. Methods This anonymous cross-sectional online survey used outcome-specific analytic populations. All 412 eligible respondents were included in discontinuation-related analyses, and the primary persistence analysis included 289 respondents who were still receiving Peg-IFN. The main outcomes included whether respondents had ever wanted to stop Peg-IFN due to adverse effects and a four-item persistence/value intention score. Psychological distress was assessed using the Patient Health Questionnaire-4 (PHQ-4). Results Among 412 eligible respondents, 175 (42.5%) had wanted to stop Peg-IFN because of adverse effects, 136 (33.0%) had asked a physician about dose reduction or discontinuation, and 39 (9.5%) reported actual premature discontinuation. In the adjusted analysis, adverse-effect burden (odds ratio 1.86 per standard deviation (SD), 95% confidence interval 1.37–2.51) and the PHQ-4 score (odds ratio 1.76, 95% confidence interval 1.28–2.41) were associated with a history of adverse-effect-related discontinuation thoughts. Among 289 currently treated respondents, treatment belief ( β = 0.280, 95% confidence interval 0.198–0.362) and physician–patient communication ( β = 0.098, 95% confidence interval 0.017–0.179) were associated with higher persistence/value intention, while the PHQ-4 score was inversely associated with this outcome ( β = −0.081, 95% confidence interval −0.148 to −0.013). Conclusion Adverse-effect burden and current psychological distress were associated with a history of adverse-effect-related discontinuation thoughts, whereas treatment belief and physician–patient communication were associated with higher persistence/value intention among patients still receiving therapy. Prospective studies are needed to evaluate whether structured education, symptom and distress screening, and tiered follow-up improve the rates of treatment completion.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本研究调查了在接受附加peginterferon alfa-2b(Peg-IFN)治疗的慢性乙型肝炎(慢性乙型肝炎)患者中,患者报告的与治疗负担、沟通和持续治疗意愿相关的因素。核心问题是不良反应负担和心理压力是否与中断治疗的想法相关,以及治疗信念和医患沟通是否与持续治疗意愿相关。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本横断面研究使用了匿名在线调查,并基于结果分析了特定人群。主要的持续分析包括289名仍在接受Peg-IFN治疗的受访者,而中断相关分析包括所有412名符合条件的受访者。主要结果包括受访者是否因不良反应想要停止Peg-IFN治疗,以及一个包含四项的持续/价值意愿评分。心理压力通过患者健康问卷-4(PHQ-4)进行评估。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 不良反应负担和当前心理压力与不良反应相关中断治疗的想法有关。相比之下,治疗信念和医患沟通与仍在接受治疗的患者更高的持续/价值意愿相关。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 本研究未探讨HBV基因型对治疗负担或持续治疗意愿的潜在影响。此外,它也未研究其他因素如社会经济状况、文化影响或治疗依从策略在塑造患者行为中的作用。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 需要前瞻性研究来评估结构化教育、症状和压力筛查以及分级随访是否能提高治疗治疗的完成率。这些干预措施对于支持患者应对Peg-IFN治疗的挑战可能是关键的。

papers.title: Testing for hepatitis C virus and hepatitis B virus/hepatitis D virus: Current scenarios and perspectives in Italy
papers.abstract: Liver disease accounts for approximately 4% of all deaths worldwide, and viral hepatitis affects more than 300 million people.The World Health Organization aims to reduce new hepatitis infections by 90% and deaths by 65% by 2030 through vaccination and screening programs.In Italy, screening for hepatitis C virus (HCV) benefits from dedicated government funding, whereas testing for hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis D virus (HDV) is supported by recommendations from scientific societies but does not benefit from dedicated national public health programmes.This expert-opinion review summarises the experience of tertiary-level Italian centres actively engaged in hospitalbased testing for HCV, HBV, and HDV and identifies practical pathways to improve testing and linkage to care.This article presents proposals to improve the effectiveness of viral hepatitis management in Italy by: (1) Strengthening coordination between hospital units and integrating information systems between general practitioners and hospitals;(2) Implementing a centralised reporting system and a structured referral network to ensure that patients with positive test results receive appropriate therapies in a timely manner; (3) Providing the resources needed to increase testing in public addiction treatment services (Servizi per le Dipendenze) and prisons; (4) Promoting screening in high-risk populations, including vulnerable and older populations; and (5) Implementing a national awareness campaign on viral hepatitis.These measures could help Italy make concrete progress towards eliminating HCV infection and controlling HBV/HDV infection within the next decade.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, genotypes, and associated diseases. It examines the current testing scenarios and management strategies for HBV in Italy, with an emphasis on improving testing and linkage to care. The central question is how to enhance the effectiveness of viral hepatitis management in Italy, particularly for HBV, through coordinated efforts and targeted interventions.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is an expert-opinion piece summarizing the experience of tertiary-level Italian centers involved in hospital-based testing for HBV, HCV, and HDV. It does not report on specific databases, search dates, eligibility criteria, or meta-analysis methods. The review is based on the authors' expertise and the practices observed in Italian healthcare settings.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review highlights the need for improved coordination between hospital units and general practitioners, the implementation of centralized reporting systems, and the expansion of testing in high-risk populations. It also emphasizes the importance of providing resources to public addiction treatment services and prisons to enhance HBV testing and management. These measures are proposed to help Italy achieve its goals of eliminating HCV infection and controlling HBV/HDV infection within the next decade.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not report on controversies or evidence gaps specific to HBV. It focuses on identifying practical pathways to improve testing and management without addressing conflicting findings or unresolved mechanisms related to HBV.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review proposes specific priorities for research, surveillance, and practice, including strengthening coordination between hospital units and general practitioners, implementing a centralized reporting system, increasing testing in public addiction treatment services and prisons, promoting screening in high-risk populations, and launching a national awareness campaign on viral hepatitis. These recommendations aim to improve the effectiveness of HBV management in Italy.

analysis.summary_en: This expert-opinion review addresses the current testing scenarios and management strategies for hepatitis B virus (HBV) in Italy. It highlights the importance of HBV testing and the need for improved coordination between hospital units and general practitioners. The review proposes measures such as implementing a centralized reporting system, increasing testing in high-risk populations, and launching a national awareness campaign to enhance HBV management. These recommendations aim to support Italy's efforts to control HBV infection and align with its public health goals. The review does not report on controversies or evidence gaps but focuses on actionable priorities for research and practice.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述聚焦于乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)感染、基因型及其相关疾病。它考察了意大利当前HBV的检测状况和管理策略,特别强调了如何通过协调努力和针对性干预来提高HBV的检测和治疗连接性。核心问题是:如何通过协调努力和针对性干预提高意大利病毒性肝炎的管理效果,特别是针对HBV。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本综述是一篇专家意见文章,总结了意大利三级医疗机构在医院内进行HBV、HCV和HDV检测的经验。它并未报告特定数据库、搜索日期、纳入标准或元分析方法。综述基于作者的专业知识和在意大利医疗环境中的观察实践。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 综述强调了改善医院单位与全科医生之间协调的必要性,实施集中报告系统,并扩大高风险人群的检测。它还强调了为公共成瘾治疗服务和监狱提供资源以增强HBV检测和管理的重要性。这些措施被提议以帮助意大利在未来十年内实现消除HCV感染和控制HBV/HDV感染的目标。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 综述未报告与HBV相关的具体争议或证据缺口。它专注于识别改进检测和管理的可行途径,而未涉及与HBV相关的矛盾发现或未解决的机制。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 综述提出了针对研究、监测和实践的具体优先事项,包括加强医院单位与全科医生之间的协调,实施集中报告系统,增加公共成瘾治疗服务和监狱中的检测,推广高风险人群的筛查,并启动全国性的病毒性肝炎意识宣传活动。这些建议旨在提高意大利HBV的管理效果。

analysis_en.scope_and_question: The review focuses on hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, genotypes, and associated diseases. It examines the current testing scenarios and management strategies for HBV in Italy, with an emphasis on improving testing and linkage to care. The central question is how to enhance the effectiveness of viral hepatitis management in Italy, particularly for HBV, through coordinated efforts and targeted interventions.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is an expert-opinion piece summarizing the experience of tertiary-level Italian centers involved in hospital-based testing for HBV, HCV, and HDV. It does not report on specific databases, search dates, eligibility criteria, or meta-analysis methods. The review is based on the authors' expertise and the practices observed in Italian healthcare settings.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review highlights the need for improved coordination between hospital units and general practitioners, the implementation of centralized reporting systems, and the expansion of testing in high-risk populations. It also emphasizes the importance of providing resources to public addiction treatment services and prisons to enhance HBV testing and management. These measures are proposed to help Italy achieve its goals of eliminating HCV infection and controlling HBV/HDV infection within the next decade.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not report on controversies or evidence gaps specific to HBV. It focuses on identifying practical pathways to improve testing and management without addressing conflicting findings or unresolved mechanisms related to HBV.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: The review proposes specific priorities for research, surveillance, and practice, including strengthening coordination between hospital units and general practitioners, implementing a centralized reporting system, increasing testing in public addiction treatment services and prisons, promoting screening in high-risk populations, and launching a national awareness campaign on viral hepatitis. These recommendations aim to improve the effectiveness of HBV management in Italy.

papers.title_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒和乙型肝炎病毒/丁型肝炎病毒检测:意大利当前状况与展望
papers.source_body_en: Liver disease accounts for approximately 4% of all deaths worldwide, and viral hepatitis affects more than 300 million people.The World Health Organization aims to reduce new hepatitis infections by 90% and deaths by 65% by 2030 through vaccination and screening programs.In Italy, screening for hepatitis C virus (HCV) benefits from dedicated government funding, whereas testing for hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis D virus (HDV) is supported by recommendations from scientific societies but does not benefit from dedicated national public health programmes.This expert-opinion review summarises the experience of tertiary-level Italian centres actively engaged in hospitalbased testing for HCV, HBV, and HDV and identifies practical pathways to improve testing and linkage to care.This article presents proposals to improve the effectiveness of viral hepatitis management in Italy by: (1) Strengthening coordination between hospital units and integrating information systems between general practitioners and hospitals;(2) Implementing a centralised reporting system and a structured referral network to ensure that patients with positive test results receive appropriate therapies in a timely manner; (3) Providing the resources needed to increase testing in public addiction treatment services (Servizi per le Dipendenze) and prisons; (4) Promoting screening in high-risk populations, including vulnerable and older populations; and (5) Implementing a national awareness campaign on viral hepatitis.These measures could help Italy make concrete progress towards eliminating HCV infection and controlling HBV/HDV infection within the next decade.

papers.title: Hepatic Steatosis in People With Chronic Hepatitis B in Africa: Prevalence, Correlates, and Clinical Significance.
papers.abstract: To address data gaps around metabolic liver disease in Africa, within the Hepatitis B in Africa Collaborative Network (HEPSANET), we evaluated participants with chronic hepatitis B virus infection (CHB) for steatotic liver disease (SLD) using transient elastography with controlled attenuation parameter (CAP). Using multivariable logistic regression, we identified sociodemographic, anthropometric, and clinical associations with SLD (CAP ≥ 248 dB/m), and evaluated whether SLD severity was independently associated with fibrosis. Short-term impacts of SLD on mortality were also assessed with Cox proportional hazards analysis. We also evaluated the diagnostic performance of B-mode ultrasound for SLD, with CAP as reference. Across 6 countries and 1601 participants (age range, 12-80 years; 39.5% female; 4% with diabetes; 11% unhealthy alcohol use; median body mass index, 24.4), 421 (26.3%) had SLD; 219 (13.7%) had severe steatosis (CAP ≥ 280 dB/m). Older age, male sex, overweight and obesity, and HIV-negative status were associated with SLD. After adjusting for age, sex, HIV status, HBV treatment, and country, severe steatosis, but not mild and moderate forms (i.e., 248-279 dB/m), was associated with a 8.4% (95%, 1.9%-14.9%) increased probability of fibrosis. Over limited follow-up (median 2.69 years) and small number of deaths, SLD was not associated with all-cause or liver-related mortality. B-mode ultrasound had low sensitivity for SLD, overall or when severe, but specificity was 95%. In conclusion, SLD was common in people with CHB in Africa and its severe form was associated with liver fibrosis. These data support screening for metabolic comorbidities as part of HBV care and treatment in Africa.
authors: Hepatitis B in Africa Collaborative Network (HEPSANET)
