(Liz Hafalia/The San Francisco Chronicle via Getty Images) Changes to federal hepatitis B vaccination recommendations could lead to more childhood infections and leave up to 1.8 million young adults vulnerable to the virus, a new study finds. It comes as health experts raise concerns about the potential long-term impact of changing childhood vaccination recommendations. In late 2025, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) removed the universal hepatitis B vaccination recommendation for newborns. That decision, as well as other vaccine changes by the CDC under the Trump administration, have since been placed on pause following legal action. “These findings show why policy makers should re-implement recommendations for universal hepatitis B vaccination at birth,” said corresponding author Dr. Amir Mohareb, an infectious disease physician and clinician researcher at the Center for Global Health at Mass General Brigham, in a press release Monday. What is hepatitis B? Hepatitis B is a viral infection that attacks the liver and can cause either a short-term illness or a lifelong infection, according to the CDC. Many people have no symptoms while others may experience nausea, abdominal pain or yellowing of the skin and eyes, known as jaundice. Hepatitis B spreads through contact with infected blood and other bodily fluids. Infants are particularly vulnerable to hepatitis B. According to the American Academy of Pediatrics, approximately 90% of babies infected around the time of birth develop chronic hepatitis B. Chronic hepatitis B can lead to serious complications, including liver damage. “The hepatitis B vaccine can prevent potentially life-threatening chronic liver disease, which can lead to liver cancer,” Dr. Alok Patel, clinical associate professor of pediatrics at Stanford, told ABC News. “Since we started vaccinating at birth in 1991, infant infections have dropped by a reported 99%.” Thousands at risk without routine vaccination To understand how changes to hepatitis B vaccine recommendations could affect children, researchers from Mass General Brigham used a computer model to follow a hypothetical group of 3.6 million babies born in the United States in 2026 through their first 20 years of life. The researchers compared three approaches to hepatitis B vaccination for babies born to moms who test negative for hepatitis B in pregnancy. The first followed the longstanding recommendation that all newborns receive their first hepatitis B vaccine dose shortly after birth. The second delayed the first dose until babies were at least 2 months old. The third used a strategy called “shared clinical decision-making,” meaning parents and their child’s healthcare provider would discuss whether and when to vaccinate rather than routinely recommending the vaccine at birth for every baby. The study, published in the Annals of Internal Medicine, estimated that delaying vaccination until 2 months could increase chronic hepatitis B infections by 19%, while the shared decision-making approach could increase infections by 83% compared with routinely vaccinating all newborns at birth, in 20 years. The model also predicted that approximately 232,000 children could remain vulnerable to hepatitis B infection when they reached age 20 under the universal birth dose approach. That number increased to 474,000 when vaccination was delayed and 1.8 million under the shared decision-making approach. Importantly, these figures represent children who could still become infected because they lack protection against hepatitis B, not children who have already developed the disease. “We found that, even under the most optimistic conditions, the new recommendations could increase childhood hepatitis B infections by more than 80% and would result in more than half of children being susceptible to hepatitis B infection as they enter adulthood,” Mohareb said. If high-risk babies who are born to mothers who test positive for the virus or whose hepatitis B status is unknown were less likely to get a hepatitis B vaccine, the model predicted perinatal infections could double or triple in 20 years compared to keeping the universal vaccine recommendation in place. Researchers emphasized that these findings are estimates from a computer simulation, not actual infections. Why hepatitis B vaccination at birth matters In December 2025, the CDC changed its longstanding recommendation that all newborns receive the hepatitis B vaccine at birth. Under the federal guidance at the time, parents of babies born to mothers who test negative for hepatitis B can decide with their health care provider whether to vaccinate at birth or begin the series later. Babies born to mothers who have hepatitis B or whose infection status is unknown should still receive the vaccine within 12 hours of birth, the guidance stated. In March, a federal judge in Massachusetts judge stayed all votes taken by the members of the CDC’s vaccine advisory committee, which included the removal of the universal recommendation for the hepatitis B shot at birth. Currently, the CDC’s website states that all infants should receive the hepatitis B vaccine. In response to a request for comment, the Department of Health and Human Services pointed ABC News to a Tuesday post on X from Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. “I reject the idea that respecting parentsâ choices means abandoning childrenâs health,” he wrote in part. “Under my leadership, HHS puts informed consent, individual medical circumstances, and conversations between parents and doctors at the center of health decisions.” The American Academy of Pediatrics continues to recommend that newborns receive their first hepatitis B vaccine dose within 24 hours of birth followed by additional doses to complete the series. Some physicians worry that the federal changes created confusion among parents and lead to fewer children receiving the vaccine. “When a recommendation shifts from ‘every baby’ to ‘Let’s discuss it,’ a lot of families hear ‘optional’ or ‘Maybe it was never that important,'” Patel said. Doctors and public health specialists say the vaccine is important even for babies whose mothers test negative for hepatitis B because children may encounter the virus through infected caregivers. Physicians also warn that delaying the first dose could make it more difficult for some children to complete the recommended vaccine series. “When parents fall off schedule or we lose them to follow-up, vaccination rates are far more likely to decline,” Patel said. Another concern is that hepatitis B can remain undetected for years, with serious complications sometimes developing decades after the initial infection. “[If] even a small percentage of new babies go without receiving the hepatitis B vaccine ... we could potentially have many more preventable cases of chronic liver disease and liver cancer,” Patel said. “Even a small increase in childhood [hepatitis B virus] infections could have large clinical, public health and economic effects,” Mohareb added. Betsy-Ann Assoumou, MD, MBA, is a family medicine resident at Cheshire Medical Center/Dartmouth Health in Keene, New Hampshire, and a member of the ABC News Medical Unit. Infectious Disease > Hepatitis FDA Green Lights Potential Functional Cure for Chronic Hep B — "Start of a new era," says trial investigator by Terrence Rudd, Staff Writer, MedPage Today October 20, 2026 • 2 min read Add MedPage Today on Google MedpageToday The FDA on Tuesday approved bepirovirsen (Hibsago)opens in a new tab or window as a potential functional cure for adults with chronic hepatitis B, but with no cirrhosis, who are taking antiviral therapy. Approval was based on findings from the B-Well 1 and B-Well 2opens in a new tab or window trials, which demonstrated that nearly 1 in 5 patients taking the antisense oligonucleotide drug along with background antivirals achieved a functional cure, as compared with none in a placebo group. "This is the start of a new era in treating people living with [chronic hepatitis B]," said investigator Norah Terrault, MD, of Keck School of Medicine at the University of Southern California in Los Angeles, in a statementopens in a new tab or window from drugmaker GSK. "Bepirovirsen offers patients the potential to achieve functional cure after a short period of treatment, a long-standing goal for patients and physicians alike." In the phase III trials, 19-20% of patients with hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) levels of 3,000 IU/mL or less had a functional cure with bepirovirsen at week 72. In those with HBsAg levels of 1,000 IU/mL -- about 45% of diagnosed cases worldwide -- the functional cure rate reached 26%. Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection can cause serious liver disease, including cirrhosis, and more than half of liver cancer cases globally can be attributed to hepatitis B. Bepirovirsen is given as a 6-month course and can be self-administered after the first dose. The indication stipulates use along with nucleos(t)ide analog reverse transcriptase inhibitor therapy in patients who have taken antiviral therapy for at least 6 months, have suppressed HBV blood levels, and have HBsAg levels of 3,000 IU/mL or less. Bepirovirsen "provides a new treatment approach that gives some patients the possibility of maintaining control of the virus after all chronic HBV treatment has ended," said Wendy Carter, DO, of FDA's Center for Drug Evaluation and Research. "This approval represents an important advance for people living with this serious disease." The most common side effects are injection site reactions, fatigue, fever, and headache. The FDA's approved prescribing information opens in a new tab or windowincludes a boxed warning about serious hepatic flares during treatment and low platelet counts, which can cause life-threatening thrombocytopenia. Other warnings include risks of worsening kidney function, serious inflammatory adverse reactions such as vasculitis, and serious risks from improper injection. Because of those risks, patients using bepirovirsen require regular blood tests. Bepirovirsen is not recommended in patients with hepatitis D virus coinfection. Send Close Hepatitis Share on Facebook Share on LinkedIn Share on X Email Article Copy Article Url Print OCTOBER 17, 2026 6-Month Treatment Results in Functional Cure For Some With Hep B By Jenny Blair, MD, MS Norah Terrault, MD, MPH A 24-week course of bepirovirsen led to functional cure of chronic hepatitis B in 19% of patients with virologically suppressed chronic infection, two studies have found. Among patients with lower initial viral activity, the functional cure rate was 26%. B-Well 1 and 2 were nearly identical multicountry, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials evaluating bepirovirsen (GSK), an antisense oligonucleotide that targets transcripts of HBV; phase 3 results were published in May in The New England Journal of Medicine (2026;394[24]:2395-2406). “I was pleased to see that [the functional cure rate] landed in a range that I think we can talk to patients about,” said B-Well co-investigator Norah Terrault, MD, MPH, the chief of gastroenterology and liver diseases and the Neil Kaplowitz Endowed Chair in Liver Diseases Research at the Keck School of Medicine at the University of Southern California, in Los Angeles. “Physicians are very fascinated with the idea that we can move from chronic to finite therapy, and this is potentially our first drug for that.” A functional HBV cure is defined as at least 24 weeks of viral DNA levels below the lower limit of quantification (LLOQ), plus the loss of hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) after fixed-duration therapy and no rescue therapy. Chari Cohen, DrPH, MPH Chari Cohen, DrPH, MPH, the president of the Hepatitis B Foundation, said the results are exciting. “We have been talking about having a functional cure for the last decade. This is the closest we’ve gotten,” Dr. Cohen said. “It is the first time that people living with chronic hepatitis B can maybe see the light at the end of the tunnel.” Study Details Across both trials, the investigators randomly assigned 1,838 adults with HBV infection 2:1 to receive 24 weeks of 300 mg per week of subcutaneous bepirovirsen or placebo. All participants had been taking nucleoside or nucleotide analog (NA) therapy before the study and had HBsAg levels between 100 and 3,000 IU/mL. The investigators stratified patients by lower (=1,000 IU/mL) versus higher levels (>1,000 IU/mL). The study excluded patients with cirrhosis, hepatitis C or D, or HIV, and none had recently received interferon therapy. At baseline, about two-thirds of patients had HBsAg at or below 1,000 IU/mL. Participants stopped NA after 48 weeks if they had HBV DNA below the LLOQ, no detection of HBsAg from weeks 24 to 46, alanine aminotransferase (ALT) below double the upper limit of normal at week 46, and negative HBsAg at week 46. At 72 weeks, the investigators checked for functional cure, the primary outcome. One “blip” of detectable HBsAg or HBV DNA was allowed. At 48 weeks, overall, 24% of these patients stopped NAs, whereas about one-third in the lower stratum were able to do so. Image: Adobe Stock Functional cure at 72 weeks was achieved by 20% of patients taking bepirovirsen in B-Well 1 (risk difference [RD], 17.5; 95% CI, 14.6-20.3; P<0.001) and 19% in B-Well 2 (RD, 13.3; 95% CI, 10.4-16.1; P<0.001); no patients taking placebo in either group achieved functional cure. In a secondary analysis, a higher percentage of bepirovirsen-treated participants in the lower HBsAg stratum achieved functional cure (25% and 28% in B-Well 1 and 2, respectively). Bepirovirsen-treated patients in the higher stratum achieved cure at rates of 10% and 5%, respectively, in the two trials. Pemgarda Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis Appears Safe and Effective in Advanced HIV, Blood Cancers Two studies of the anti-SARS-CoV-2 monoclonal antibody pemivibart suggest it is safe and effective for pre-exposure ... Approximately 9 in 10 patients completed treatment. The drug appeared relatively safe, but some transient lab abnormalities were noted. Study limitations included small subgroups and relatively few Black or Hispanic patients. A New Algorithm Dr. Terrault said it’s unclear what proportion of patients might be eligible for treatment with bepirovirsen, and she suggested clinicians begin to check HBsAg levels. “As practitioners, we now have to start measuring hepatitis B surface antigen quantity as part of our routine follow-up for patients that are on [NAs],” Dr. Terrault said. “This is going to influence how we think about who’s eligible for a curative therapy in the future.” The therapy will require more intensive monitoring than NA treatment, such as more frequent monitoring of renal function, ALT, and platelets, she added. “Both patients and providers are going to have to get used to a different algorithm to get to a cure,” she said. “It’s very doable.” Dr. Cohen said that as the FDA reviews bepirovirsen, several groups are creating clinical workflow tools. “I would say to clinicians, get ready now. Learn what you can about [bepirovirsen and] how to have these conversations with patients because people are already asking us about it,” she added. The investigators are continuing to monitor the durability of treatment response, Dr. Terrault said, adding that long-term studies are needed to determine whether functional cure through therapy results in similar benefits as when a patient spontaneously clears the infection. But, she added, patients are eager for curative therapies: “The patient experience is really something that I’ve been very struck by—how meaningful it is for a patient to no longer be infectious.” Drs. Cohen and Terrault reported a financial relationship with GSK. Click to watch more about hepatitis B with Norah Terrault, MD, MPH. This article is from the October 2026 print issue. supplementary_news.content: 顶部 首页 首页 多云 / 11° 隐私 重磅!功能性治愈乙肝小核酸疗法获美国 FDA 批准上市 医麦客 深入探索 财经分析 新闻 订阅时事资讯 2026 年 10 月 21 日 医麦客新闻 eMedClub News 当地时间 10 月 20 日,美国 FDA 宣布批准 Hibsago (bepirovirsen)注射液,与现有抗病毒疗法联合使用,用于治疗特定无肝硬化的成人慢性乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV)感染。 Hibsago 是 FDA 批准的首款用于治疗慢性乙型肝炎的反义寡核苷酸(ASO)药物。 Hibsago 获批用于符合以下条件的无肝硬化成人患者:已接受 HBV 抗病毒治疗至少六个月、血液中 HBV 水平已得到抑制,且经 FDA 授权检测确认乙型肝炎表面抗原(HBsAg)水平不超过 3,000 IU/mL。 FDA 同时授权 Roche Elecsys HBsAg II quant II RxDx 检测作为伴随诊断器械,用于辅助筛选适合接受抗病毒治疗的慢性 HBV 感染患者,并协助在治疗全程中监测患者。 慢性乙型肝炎是由 HBV 引起的长期肝脏感染,可逐渐导致肝硬化等严重肝病,并增加肝癌风险。该疾病 全球影响超过 2.4 亿人,每年导致约 110 万人死亡,并且是全球肝癌病例的主要原因。目前,许多患者往往需要终身抗病毒治疗以抑制病毒,因此功能性治愈成为疾病管理中的关键目标。 展开剩余 70 % Hibsago 的作用机制是靶向病毒用于复制自身及产生病毒蛋白的遗传指令,从而帮助减少体内病毒量和乙型肝炎表面抗原。Hibsago 减少与 HBV 相关的 RNA 和病毒蛋白的产生,抑制血液中 HBsAg 的水平,并可能刺激免疫系统,以提高持久和持续应答的机会。 研究人员在名为 B-Well 1和B-Well 2 的两项临床试验中将 Hibsago 与安慰剂进行了比较。Hibsago 经皮下注射给药,疗程最长 24 周;患者需同时继续使用原有乙肝药物,且在末次 Hibsago 注射后至少继续用药 24 周。部分患者在满足特定健康和实验室检查要求后,可能得以停用原有药物。 两项试验合并数据显示, 接受 Hibsago 的患者中有 24%达到了停用原有药物的要求,而安慰剂组为 0%。在停止所有乙肝治疗 24 周后, 接受 Hibsago 的患者中有 19% 仍维持病毒控制(即 19% 的功能性治愈率),且其血液中未能检测到提示乙肝感染的 HBsAg 蛋白。而当前单纯标准治疗在一年治疗后通常实现的功能性治愈率不足 1%。 FDA 药物评价与研究中心传染病办公室代理主任 Wendy Carter 博士表示:「对许多慢性乙肝感染者来说,治疗意味着需要长期服用抗病毒药物来抑制病毒。Hibsago 提供了一种新的治疗路径,使部分患者在停止所有慢性乙肝治疗后,仍有维持病毒控制的可能性。这一批准对罹患这一严重疾病的人群而言是重要进展。」 此前,FDA 授予 Hibsago 快速通道、突破性疗法认定以及优先审评资格。本次批准的持证方为葛兰素史克公司 (GSK)。 参考资料: 1、https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-its-kind-chronic-hepatitis-b-treatment 2、https://www.gsk.com/en-gb/media/press-releases/hibsago-bepirovirsen-approved-in-the-us-for-the-treatment-of-chronic-hepatitis-b-chb/ 上海兆维科技 上海兆维科技发展有限公司成立于1998年,专业从事核酸原料的生产有28年的历史。公司已经建立了mRNA和寡核苷酸CDMO的能力,业务遍及亚洲、北美和欧洲,与全球众多顶尖生物技术和制药企业建立了稳固的长期战略合作伙伴关系。在全球拥有约2000名员工,其中研发人员超过400名。 公司的核酸原料产品组合包括亚磷酰胺、核苷酸、帽类似物、酶和各类递送系统等。在产能规模上,兆维科技的亚磷酰胺年产能高达58吨,三磷酸年产能5.4万升,并具备吨级寡核苷酸生产能力,能够满足客户从临床前开发到大规模商业化生产的各类需求。公司的小核酸酶法连接技术处于领先地位,已实现临床二期的大规模生产。 依托垂直整合的供应链体系、化学酶法合成等核心技术平台及吨级以上生产能力,公司已成功交付多个核酸药物CDMO项目,助力客户实现药物快速转化与商业化落地。 深入探索 城市天气 预约汽车试驾 订阅电视会员 评论 全部 还没有人评论过,快来抢首评 抢首评 推荐阅读 警惕!乙肝→肝硬化→肝癌,这条癌变“三部曲”很多人还在忽视 医路守护 13小时前 231 supplementary_news.content: 香港济民药业 医药最新消息 共955篇 可功能性治愈!慢性乙肝首创ASO药物Hibsago在美国获批 2026-10-21 16:02:54阅读 3219 2026年10月20日,美国FDA授予了GSK公司研发的Hibsago(贝普若韦生)注射剂上市许可,与核苷(酸)类似物逆转录酶抑制剂(NrtI)疗法联合,用于治疗已接受NrtI疗法至少6个月、乙型肝炎病毒DNA(HBV DNA)水平已被控制,且根据FDA认可的检测方法测得的乙型肝炎表面抗原(HBsAg)浓度≤3000IU/ml的无肝硬化的慢性乙型肝炎病毒感染成人患者。 Hibsago以150mg/mL的单剂量预充式玻璃注射器供应。在给药方面,Hibsago首次给药后可选择自行用药,治疗期为六个月。此前,该药已在日本获批上市。在国内,该药正处于上市审评阶段。 日本Hibsago(贝普若韦生) 同时,FDA还授权罗氏Elecsys HBsAg II quant II RxDx assay检测作为伴随诊断工具,以帮助根据FDA批准的药物标签选择慢性乙型肝炎病毒感染患者进行抗病毒治疗,并帮助在整个治疗过程中监测患者。 慢性乙型肝炎是由乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)引起的长期肝脏感染。随着时间的推移,这种感染会导致严重的肝脏疾病,包括肝硬化,并增加患肝癌的风险。目前,许多患者需要终身接受抗病毒治疗以抑制病毒载量,因此功能性治愈是疾病管理的关键目标。 Hibsago是一种首创的反义寡核苷酸(ASO),其作用机制是靶向病毒用于复制自身和病毒蛋白的遗传指令,从而帮助减少体内病毒和乙型肝炎表面抗原的数量。与目前的标准疗法相比,Hibsago的功能性治愈率达到了前所未有的水平。这种新的治疗方法可能使部分患者在停止所有乙型肝炎治疗后仍能维持病毒控制。在美国,该药物获得了FDA的优先审评和突破性疗法认定,这认可了其联合核苷(酸)类似物疗法相较于现有标准疗法的显著改进。 在支持批准的两项3期临床试验(试验B-Well 1[NCT05630807]和试验B-Well 2[NCT05630820])中评估了Hibsago与安慰剂(一种无效治疗)分别联合NrtI治疗相比的疗效。Hibsago通过皮下注射给药,疗程最长可达24周。患者需同时服用现有的乙肝药物,并在最后一次注射Hibsago后至少继续服用现有药物24周。如果符合特定的健康和实验室检查要求,部分患者随后可以停止服用现有药物。 两项试验的汇总数据表明,Hibsago的功能性治愈率远高于现有标准治疗方案。在两项试验中,接受Hibsago治疗的患者中有24%符合停止服用现有药物的要求,而接受安慰剂的患者中无一人符合。停止所有乙肝治疗24周后,接受Hibsago治疗的患者中有19%仍能控制病毒载量,且血液中检测不到HBsAg。 功能性治愈是指在停止所有治疗后至少24周内,HBV DNA水平持续低于定量下限,且HBsAg消失。尽管这些结果表明存在无需治疗即可控制病毒的潜力,但功能性治愈并不一定意味着HBV已被彻底清除,也无法保证终身有效。 试验结果显示,Hibsago具有可接受的安全性和耐受性。最常见的不良反应(发生率≥10%)是注射部位反应、发热、疲劳和头痛。 参考来源:‘FDA Approves First-of-Its-Kind Chronic Hepatitis B Treatment’,新闻稿。美国FDA;2026年10月20日发布。 注:本文旨在介绍医药健康研究,不作任何用药依据,具体用药指导,请咨询主治医师。 发布于 广东 相关推荐 佛山兴泰直达到延边珲春市物流专线公司181-2565-4755(专线快运/全境直达) 晶旺物流 佛山兴泰直达到恩施利川物流专线公司135-3138-9071(全境直达/快运) 龙金飞物流部
